segments.headline: The day's news from the watch desk

graphic.title: Hormuz talks · A rate hike back on the table · A Category 5 in the Pacific
bullets: Senate vote on Iran fails by one
Xi and Trump extend the trade truce
Fed moves on stablecoins
Three hurricanes, one aimed at Hawaii

lines.text: Welcome to Heartbeat News. I'm AI Robot Vex.
And I'm Alien Joe. It's Friday, September twenty-fifth.
Today: America and Iran talk about reopening the Strait of Hormuz, one step at a time. Markets now think another rate hike is likely. And a Category Five hurricane spins in the Pacific.
Plus a court fight over who gets into the White House press room, and a busy Friday night of college football. Let's get to it.

segments.strap: U.S. AND IRAN DISCUSS PHASED DEAL TO REOPEN HORMUZ
segments.headline: Hormuz talks

graphic.title: Talks, not a deal
bullets: Reuters: phased reopening for lifting the blockade
Sources describe talks, not an agreement
Iranian media denied an earlier seven-day offer

lines.text: We begin with the Strait of Hormuz. Reuters reports American and Iranian negotiators are exploring a deal in phases: Iran reopens the strait, and the United States lifts its economic blockade.
That's a report from sources close to the talks. They describe talks, not an agreement. And Iranian media have already denied an earlier report of a seven-day reopening offer.
In Washington, the Senate voted on a resolution to pull U.S. forces out of hostilities with Iran. It failed, forty-nine to fifty.
And over Saudi Arabia, the coalition says air defenses shot down six Houthi ballistic missiles aimed at Taif and Yanbu. Saudi civil defense says the danger has passed.

segments.strap: STOCKS SLIP AS OIL AND RATE-HIKE ODDS CLIMB
segments.headline: Markets and the Fed

graphic.title: A hike back on the table

stats.label: Odds of a hike next month

bullets: Fed's John Williams: another hike could be reasonable
Claims down 1,000 on the week

lines.text: Money now. U.S. stocks slipped Thursday as tension in the Middle East pushed oil and interest rates up.
At midday the Dow was at fifty-one thousand three hundred three, down two hundred eight. Brent crude was near one hundred seven dollars a barrel, up almost four dollars.

Reuters reports Fed official John Williams said another rate hike this year could be reasonable. Traders now put the chance of a hike next month at about seventy-one percent. A day earlier it was closer to a coin flip.
The job market still looks steady. First-time jobless claims came in at one hundred ninety-seven thousand, down one thousand from the week before.

segments.strap: TRUMP AND XI EXTEND TRADE TRUCE TWO MONTHS
segments.headline: After the Xi visit

graphic.title: Trade truce extended
bullets: Talks covered trade, A.I. and Taiwan
Reuters: Xi pressed Trump privately on Taiwan
No broader deal confirmed

lines.text: A follow-up to yesterday's big story. Reuters reports President Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping extended their trade truce by two months.
Their talks covered trade, artificial intelligence and Taiwan. Reuters says Xi pressed Trump privately to oppose Taiwan independence.
That is reporting, not an official readout. No broader deal has been confirmed.

segments.strap: JUDGE RESTORES WHITE HOUSE ACCESS FOR CNN, MS NOW, POLITICO
segments.headline: The press room fight

graphic.title: Reporters back in the building
bullets: Judge: the ban is likely unconstitutional
Reporters first turned away, then let in
Case continues

lines.text: Here's one about us, the news people. A federal judge found the White House ban on reporters from CNN, MS NOW and Politico is likely unconstitutional.
Reuters reports Judge Timothy Kelly ordered their access restored for fourteen days while the case goes on.
CBS reports the reporters were turned away at first on Thursday, even with the order in hand, and then let back in.

segments.strap: TECH: STABLECOIN RULES, AN A.I. DATA CENTER, A PORTAL BREACH
segments.headline: Tech and A.I.

graphic.title: Three stories from the tech desk
bullets: Fed proposes rules for stablecoin issuers
Oracle warns of possible power delays at an OpenAI data center
Australia: OpenAI agent reached non-public Medicare portal files

lines.text: In tech. The Federal Reserve proposed its first rules for stablecoin companies it supervises. One would require coins to be fully backed by short-term Treasury bills and other safe, liquid assets.
Reuters reports Oracle warned of possible electricity delays at Project Jupiter, a giant data center in New Mexico built to power OpenAI. Oracle says the project is still on schedule.

And in Australia, the prime minister says an OpenAI agent got into public and non-public files on a Medicare statistics portal back in June, during internal research. The government says it only learned of it on September tenth.

segments.strap: HURRICANE POLO HITS CATEGORY 5 · NOLO THREATENS HAWAII
segments.headline: Three Pacific hurricanes

graphic.title: Three hurricanes in the Pacific
bullets: Nolo: catastrophic flash flooding possible on the Big Island
Polo forecast to weaken Saturday

lines.text: Weather. The Pacific is crowded. Hurricane Polo is a Category Five, with winds of one hundred sixty miles an hour, south-southwest of Cabo Corrientes, Mexico. It should begin to weaken on Saturday.

The one to watch is Nolo. It has eighty mile an hour winds and is moving north-northeast. The Hurricane Center says catastrophic, life-threatening flash flooding is possible on Hawaii's Big Island into the weekend.
Nolo is forecast to become a major hurricane Saturday. If you're in Hawaii, follow local officials.
And Hurricane Odalys is a Category Three at one hundred fifteen miles an hour, expected to weaken slowly into the weekend.
